title: Repurchase Agreements

maps.tested: Rated Very Important. Reported once with an unusual framing that tests the counterparty relationship rather than the arithmetic.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'repo calculation: which party is more vulnerable if one bank is not allowing the repo to roll over?' The candidate's own answer was the hedge fund. Closed-book settlement amount: [(price + accrued) x (1 - haircut)] x (1 + repo x t). This template is confirmed to recur across GARP practice papers.

vardeezReading: LTR-13: Very Important. "For this, understand general collateral, special collateral and LO78F. Special spreads and the auction cycle."

los.vardeez: Special spreads and the auction cycle (his "LO 78.f")

selectors.name: Repo settlement amount and repurchase price
selectors.what: Cash lent at initiation = (clean price + accrued interest) x (1 - haircut), on the invoice value of the collateral; repurchase price at the unwind = cash lent x (1 + repo rate x days/360). Closed-book template: [(price + accrued) x (1 - haircut)] x (1 + repo x t).
selectors.theory: Why the collateral is valued at the invoice (full) price, including accrued interest; why the haircut makes the cash lent smaller than the collateral value and is funded by the borrower of cash from its own capital (invoice value x haircut); why the repurchase price is the cash lent plus repo interest on an actual/360 basis.

selectors.name: Who is vulnerable if the repo is not rolled
selectors.what: Given a repo where one bank will not roll it over, decide which party is more exposed: the borrower of cash, who must refinance or fire-sell collateral, and not the lender of cash, who gets its cash back and holds over-collateralisation meanwhile. The question tests the roles in the trade rather than arithmetic.
selectors.theory: Repo funding can disappear as fast as the repos mature, mostly overnight; the loss of financing is often the killing blow for leveraged borrowers.

selectors.name: General versus special collateral
selectors.what: Compare general collateral (cash lender accepts any security in a class) with special collateral (cash lender initiates the trade to obtain a particular security): every special rate is typically below the GC rate, special spread = GC rate - special rate, and a funding trade on a bond not trading special pays the GC rate.

selectors.name: Special spreads and the auction cycle
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Special spreads and the auction cycle (his LO 78.f)'
selectors.what: Characteristics of special spreads and their typical behaviour over a Treasury auction cycle: the on-the-run issue trades most special, then the old, then the double-old; spreads are small just after an auction, rise as shorts migrate and spike into the next auction; before May 2009 the special rate could not fall below zero, so the spread was capped by the GC rate, and the TMPG fails penalty then became the cap.

notSelected: LTR-13 b (motivations: cash management, long financing, shorting through a reverse repo), LTR-13 d (Lehman and Bear Stearns), LTR-13 g (financing advantage of a special bond) and the counterparty-risk and liquidity-risk detail of LTR-13 c beyond the roll-over question carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer.
